main_body: A sci-fi metal wall face (blue-grey panels with orange trim stripe, recessed panels, a vent, and a base rail), drawn as a flat front-facing wall tile
top_band: none; the pixel column from row 0 runs through a light blue-grey strip, then a dark strip, then the wall face, then an orange stripe at rows 5-6. There is no horizontal surface visible from above.
evidence: The kind is terrain (a wall face), so a flat vertical face is plausible. But the whole drawing is a front elevation: panels, vent and shelves are vertical faces. There is no top band, only a 1-2 row trim at the top and thin rails. The recessed panels have dark inner edges, but there is no visible horizontal surface. Under the strict contract this fails.

style.evidence: The wall uses about 4 blue-grey steps (light edge, mid panel, dark, deep base) plus orange and brown accents, so it is a bit shallower than the references' 5-6 steps. The outlines are dark blue-tinted tones of the metal, not pure black. Texture is limited to a few rivet dots and small highlight dashes. The panel interiors and the lower band are large flat fills of one colour, about 5x5 px or more. Tile density is lower than the timber and stone references, which carry per-stone and grain variation. Next to the references it looks flatter and thinner.
